items.title: Classical psychedelic microdosing, mood, and cognitive function: An umbrella review with narrative synthesis.
items.summary: An umbrella review of microdosing research (sub-perceptual doses of LSD or psilocybin) found limited evidence for mood or cognitive benefits. Three meta-analyses incorporating 14 studies showed no support for cognitive enhancement; notably, microdosing was associated with a small but reliable impairment of cognitive control. Reported mood improvements did not persist under blinded conditions, suggesting expectancy effects. The authors conclude that adequately powered, preregistered, expectancy-controlled trials are needed before clinical recommendations can be made.

items.title: The purpose of the psychosocial protocol in the psychedelic-assisted therapy: A scoping review.
items.summary: A scoping review categorizes psychosocial protocols used in psychedelic-assisted therapy research across multiple dimensions: purpose, denomination, format, therapeutic orientation, formalization, and duration. The analysis synthesized experimental and observational studies examining Ayahuasca, DMT, and other psychedelics for psychiatric treatment, highlighting the importance of structured psychological support alongside substance administration in clinical research.

items.title: Increased morning cortisol after ketamine treatment for suicidal depression: Exploratory report from a randomized trial.
items.summary: A midazolam-controlled randomized trial found that subanesthetic intravenous ketamine rapidly reduced suicidal ideation within 24 hours in depressed patients. An exploratory analysis measured morning cortisol via saliva samples before and after treatment. Results showed a significant increase in waking cortisol 24 hours post-infusion (p=0.0025), with a small-to-medium nonsignificant correlation between cortisol elevation and suicidal ideation reduction (r=-0.25, p=0.052). The findings suggest that modest cortisol increases following psychedelics may enhance stress resilience, though replication is needed.

items.title: Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of orally administered S-ketamine in healthy participants.
items.summary: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study in 16 healthy participants compared oral and intravenous S-ketamine administration. Oral S-ketamine showed poor absolute bioavailability (9–12%), resulting in substantially lower S-ketamine peak plasma concentrations but disproportionately higher metabolite-to-parent ratios compared to intravenous dosing. This altered metabolite profile raises questions about whether oral S-ketamine can achieve the pharmacodynamic conditions necessary for antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant depression, despite higher oral doses. Safety and CNS effects were assessed up to 24 and 6 hours post-dose, respectively.

items.title: The intersection between psychedelics and schizophrenia spectrum disorders: Reevaluating risk and therapeutic potential.
items.summary: A narrative review examines the complex relationship between psychedelics and schizophrenia spectrum disorders, challenging the traditional "psychotomimetic" classification that equates psychedelic experiences with psychotic symptoms. While phenomenological overlap exists, qualitative differences suggest they operate through distinct neural mechanisms involving serotonergic, dopaminergic, and glutamatergic pathways. Clinical evidence confirms psychedelics can exacerbate existing psychosis and trigger symptoms in vulnerable individuals, though precise risk magnitudes remain unclear. The review suggests potential therapeutic applications for specific symptoms—notably negative symptoms and depression—in stable patients under controlled dosing, warranting careful patient selection and further investigation.

items.title: Multi-metric evaluations of acute psychedelic effects on fMRI brain entropy.
items.summary: A 28-participant study evaluated 14 brain entropy metrics using fMRI scans before and after psilocybin administration (121 total scans). Using linear mixed-effects models across two parcellation strategies and seven denoising pipelines, researchers found consistent positive associations for five entropy measures—including Shannon entropy and brain-state switching—but no significant effects for eight metrics and inconsistent results for Lempel-Ziv complexity. Weak inter-measure correlations suggest these metrics capture distinct neurobiological phenomena rather than a single construct, supporting a more nuanced understanding of psychedelics' acute effects on brain entropy.

items.title: Mechanistic insights toward dissociating therapeutic from psychedelic effects: bridging the gap between psychedelic research and mental health care.
items.summary: Clinical trials show psychedelics may treat depression and anxiety, but their intense subjective effects—including ego dissolution and altered default mode network activity—require extensive preparation and integration support, limiting scalability and excluding patients with certain psychiatric conditions. Researchers are investigating whether therapeutic benefits can be dissociated from consciousness-altering effects through pharmacological strategies targeting serotonin 2A receptors and other mechanisms, potentially expanding accessibility and clinical utility.

items.title: Oral Prolonged-Release Ketamine for Treatment-Resistant Depression: Two Randomized Clinical Trials.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated KET01, a novel oral prolonged-release ketamine formulation for treatment-resistant depression. Two randomized controlled trials tested efficacy and tolerability: KET01-03 (n=healthy volunteers, Germany) compared a single 240 mg KET01 dose to intranasal esketamine (84 mg), measuring dissociative effects via the CADSS scale. KET01-02 (n=29 sites across Central Europe) assessed KET01 at 120 or 240 mg daily versus placebo for 3 weeks in treatment-resistant depression patients, using the MADRS depression scale as primary outcome. The oral formulation aims to reduce dissociative and cardiovascular side effects associated with current ketamine-based treatments while maintaining rapid antidepressant efficacy.
